key_insight: Leaderboard scores on performance-optimization coding benchmarks can be misleading: they may reflect benchmark noise, scoring rules, and task coverage more than true agent capability. The paper argues that these benchmarks need careful auditing before being treated as reliable evidence of progress.
problem_solved: It addresses the question of whether repository-level performance-optimization benchmarks like GSO, SWE-Perf, and SWE-fficiency are actually measuring coding-agent performance reliably, or whether their scores are inflated or distorted by benchmark artifacts.
method: Audit multiple repository-level performance-optimization benchmarks and their scoring procedures.
Examine how runtime instability and benchmark-specific rules can affect reported leaderboard performance.
Analyze how benchmark coverage and the number of tasks already solved by public submissions can bias comparisons.
impact: This matters because researchers and practitioners may otherwise overestimate the real-world effectiveness of coding agents based on benchmark leaderboards. The findings encourage more robust evaluation practices and more cautious interpretation of reported gains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing benchmark input: repository patch -> runtime measurement -> leaderboard score
Bar chart comparing apparent leaderboard gains vs adjusted/robust performance
Icon-based callouts for 'runtime instability', 'scoring rules', and 'task coverage bias'
Side-by-side visual of 'benchmark score' versus 'true agent capability'
paper_title: Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?
paper_authors: Zhi Chen, Zhensu Sun, Yuling Shi, David Lo, Lingxiao Jiang
